items.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with negative adverbial fronting.
options: Never have I seen such a mess.
Never I have seen such a mess.
Never I seen such a mess have.
Never have seen I such a mess.
items.explanation: Negative fronting inverts subject and auxiliary: Never have I seen …

items.prompt: Write two words: Hardly ___ ___ arrived when the meeting started.
Choose the correct completion: Not only ___ the deadline, but they also hid the delay.
options: did they miss
they missed
they did miss
did missed they
items.explanation: 'Not only' fronting inverts: did they miss.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses fronting of the object?
options: His promises I don't believe.
I don't believe his promises.
I don't believe them.
Believing his promises is hard for me.
items.explanation: The object 'his promises' is moved to the front for emphasis.

items.prompt: Which sentence postpones the heavy subject?
options: It is hard to justify the cost.
To justify the cost is hard.
The cost to justify is hard.
Justifying the cost is what is hard.
items.explanation: The 'it' + postponed infinitive keeps the opening light.

items.prompt: Write one word: Seldom ___ the server go down during peak hours.
Why do skilled writers postpone long subjects?
options: To keep the opening of the sentence light and readable.
To make the sentence as long as possible.
To avoid using a verb at the start.
To hide the main idea from the reader.
items.explanation: Postponement moves heavy material to the end for readability.
